A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same BulletTime research work, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Appendices A–D. All content can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and real-world video-generation experiments, conditioning ablations, and baseline fine-tuning results in Tables 1–5 and D.1, alongside qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and results, including the quantitative comparisons, ablations, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Time-RoPE, Time-AdaLN, unified 4D-RoPE, and Camera-AdaLN components. The architecture, conditioning procedures, and training method are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same PointOdyssey-based synthetic data, ViPE real-world videos, fixed-camera temporal-control evaluation, and UCF101 reference distribution. No datasets, tasks, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: TrajectoryCrafter* and ReCamMaster* remain the comparison methods in Tables 1–2. The conditioning alternatives in Table 4 and released versus fine-tuned ReCamMaster comparisons in Table D.1 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The protocols remain identical: 500 synthetic evaluation videos, 100 ViPE videos, 384×640 resolution, and 81 frames. Training budgets, metrics, time-remapping procedures, and appendix evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the same camera–time disentanglement analysis, conditioning ablations, unseen timing demonstrations, failure cases, and ReCamMaster fine-tuning/time-remapping analyses in Section 4 and Appendices B/D.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Both present the same point estimates without reporting repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–5 and D.1 and all qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports the same proposed-method PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS of 24.57/0.6905/0.1265, and Table 2 retains rotation/translation errors of 1.47/1.32.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the continuous-time attention derivation, and Appendix A's explanation of equivalence to standard RoPE under uniform sampling are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about decoupled world-time/camera control, the synthetic dataset, real-world generalization, and state-of-the-art 4D-controllable video generation.

C2.justification: The mechanism interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including synthetic-data realism, long-video constraints, UCF101 distribution mismatch, and failures involving hands and unseen backgrounds.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, optimizer details, data-generation instructions, and code/data/model release statements are unchanged. The new NVIDIA Academic Grant Program acknowledgment credits GPU support but supplies no hardware specifications, revised configuration, or access instructions.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, novelty positioning, and all 85 references are unchanged. Reference entries move across columns and pages without additions, removals, or substantive revisions.

P1.justification: v2 adds one acknowledgment sentence thanking the NVIDIA Academic Grant Program for GPU resources and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining wording and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded acknowledgment causes reference entries to reflow across columns and pages 9–12, and the first-page margin stamp changes. All scientific figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds attribution for GPU support and makes associated presentation updates. The methods, empirical evidence, technical documentation, claims, and limitations—including the appendices—are unchanged, establishing no meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
